key_insight: A bismuth density functional tight binding (DFTB) model with explicit spin–orbit coupling enables topological screening at approximately 1,000 times the computational efficiency of standard DFT.
engineering_relevance: The model makes large-scale screening of strain and buckling practical for identifying bismuthene structures with promising electronic and topological properties.
method: Develop a transferable bismuth DFTB model with explicit spin–orbit coupling.
Map band-gap closure and band inversion across bismuthene strain and buckling.
Validate topology against DFT using optimized bilayers, a band-inversion order parameter, and the Z₂ invariant.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate rhombohedral band structures, transferability tests on phonon density of states and solid-phase energy ordering, and topological validation against DFT.
watch_item: Validation is specific to the studied bismuth structures; reliability beyond the tested structural range or in other materials requires further assessment.
paper_title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
